title: The assistant's tools
next: Memory, notes and what it knows

beats.text: Ask your assistant, and it {does}does it: {files}finds a file, {weather}checks the weather, {music}pauses the music. Those are its {tools}tools.
Let's see {what}what it can do, {ask}when it asks first, and how to {own}add your own.

In {settings}Settings, Tools, there are {count}more than eighty built-in tools, by subject: the {calendar}calendar, {files}files, the {internet}internet and your phone, {mail}mail, {music}music, {notes}notes and memory, {pc}programs and the PC, the {screen}screen and texts, and more.

It doesn't hand all of them to the AI: it {picks}picks the ones that fit what you ask. {off}Switch off the ones you don't want, and it chooses better among the rest. And {test}Test tries any of them right away.
In the assistant's options, {before}Ask before doing something: {never}never, {risky}only what's risky, like shutting down, scripts or keys, or {first}also the first time.
And {each}each tool can have its own: {safe}without asking, {once}the first time, or {always}always.
When it asks, answer by click or by voice: {yes}yes, {no}no, or {always}yes, and don't ask again. And if something wasn't what you wanted, say {undo}undo that.

Make your own in {custom}Custom: {file}one file per tool, to query a {web}website or an API, run one of your {commands}commands, do {steps}several steps in a row, or run a {script}script. They {load}load by themselves when you save the file.
Or plug in {mcp}MCP servers, with all their tools. They {start}start when an assistant needs them, and {stop}stop on their own. And their keys go in {secrets}Secrets.

One last tip: it works the other way, too. In {share}Share, {programs}Claude Desktop, VS Code or Open WebUI can use your assistants' tools and your K-Desktop commands. {copy}Copy the configuration, paste it into the program, and that's it.
